title: How this draft was checked
body: A session agent redrafted the page from its blueprint for #71. A fresh fact-checker read 108 claims: 105 held and 3 were imprecise. The register editor's 28 findings, 4 blocking, were applied, and a recheck's lines were fixed.

The blueprint was brought in line with the reviewed page after you approved it, so a later redraft keeps every fix. Each change rests on the code or a fact, and none changes the page's sections or the reader's path.

title: Two hand-written steps cairn now does for you
body: The old page had the reader write a dev-build Vite plugin and declare its flag in `app.d.ts`. `cairnManifest` now defines the flag, and `@glw907/cairn-cms/ambient` declares it, so both steps are gone.

title: What is Waymark called?
body: Waymark has no entry in the register's Names list. The facts call it a template and the pages call it a theme. This page now says "cairn's reference reading theme". Whatever you pick becomes a Names entry and a Vale rule.

choices.label: Template for the copy, theme for its look
choices.done: The session adds a Names entry that says "template" for what the setup command copies and "theme" for its look, and aligns the pages.

choices.label: Theme everywhere
choices.done: The session adds the Names entry and rewords the facts.

choices.label: Template everywhere
choices.done: The session adds the Names entry and rewords the pages.

title: "The App" as a short name
body: After first use, the page shortens the GitHub App to "the App", a short name the Names list doesn't sanction. The session left it as is.

choices.label: Keep "the App"
choices.done: The page stands, and the session adds the short name to the Names list.

choices.label: Use the full name
choices.done: The session writes "the GitHub App" every time and reruns the gate.
